Subject: Verdant Health: CAIQ mapping & network boundary narrative request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. Verdant is doing an internal SIG/CAIQ run and our compliance team has asked for a concise network boundary narrative that explains how Redwood's Dedicated/private deployment model maps to CAIQ items related to network isolation, ingress/egress controls, and key management. In particular they asked for: 

- A short (1-2 page) narrative that we can attach to the CAIQ explaining tenant isolation, control plane boundaries, and egress filtering.
- An annotated VPC/network diagram for both the Dedicated and Private (customer-managed VPC) patterns showing firewalls, NAT, KMS boundaries, and any peering gateways.
- A CAIQ mapping spreadsheet that indicates which Redwood artifacts or controls correspond to CAIQ rows (a couple of example rows filled is fine).

Target: our audit window is the week of Apr 19, so if you can share initial artifacts early next week that would be ideal. Also please flag any gaps where you need runbooks, logs, or screenshots from us.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call after you've had a chance to draft.

Alex
Alex Ng
Security Architect, Verdant Health
alex.ng@verdanthealth.com

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver the items you listed. Planned deliverables and cadence: 

1) Boundary narrative (PDF) — 1–2 pages, non-technical summary + technical appendix.
2) Annotated diagrams — two artifacts: Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool) and Private (customer VPC with Redwood edge).
3) CAIQ mapping workbook — spreadsheet with CAIQ rows mapped to Redwood controls, evidence pointers, and related links.

Clarifying Qs: 
- For Private deployment, are you expecting Redwood to run the control plane in your VPC (customer-controlled) or to connect via a dedicated peering/edge? If you confirm we will annotate both paths but focus the narrative on your preferred model.
- Do you need SOC 2 control crosswalks as a separate sheet, or is a single workbook with CAIQ + SOC2 tabs acceptable?

I'll pull a quick sketch and an initial CAIQ template. Looping in Karthik and Vanessa to produce the technical diagram and the SOC 2 crosswalk. Target: initial draft (sketch + CAIQ template) by Apr 12 COB, full package by Apr 13 morning.

Subject: Re: Verdant Health: CAIQ mapping & network boundary narrative request

Alex / Irene — attaching the first-pass mapping and a more detailed diagram turned into a PDF. High-level notes to include in the narrative: 

- Tenant isolation: Dedicated mode uses GPU pools isolated by tenant VLANs and tenant-aware scheduling. Control plane (management plane) is logically separated from customer data plane; control plane APIs are reachable from Redwood admin subnets only and protected by mTLS. For Private deployments where the customer provides the VPC, Redwood runs a lightweight agent in the customer's VPC and establishes an authenticated, mutual TLS tunnel to Redwood's control endpoints.

- Network boundaries: We place network ACLs at the edge and implement egress allowlists per-tenant. Traffic destined for customer endpoints is routed through NAT gateways in the customer's VPC for Private deployments, and through Redwood-managed egress gateways for Dedicated hosted pools.

- KMS & keys: Data at rest within model artifacts and customer data blobs is encrypted using customer-managed keys (CMKs) when requested; otherwise Redwood-managed KMS is used. KMS access is scoped by IAM roles and audited. Key usage logs are surfaced for SOC 2 evidence.

- Logging/evidence: flow logs (VPC flow logs), audit logs (control plane API audit), and host-level process logs are available. We can provide sample exports and retention settings per your audit policy.

Attachments: CAIQ-Redwood-Verdant-20270412.xlsx, SOC2-control-mapping-verdant-20270412.xlsx, redwood_vpc_prod_nonprod_v1.pdf

Irene — if you want, I can redline the CAIQ sheet with exact CAIQ IDs where we map controls.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Let's do a 45-minute walkthrough on Apr 14. Can one of you send an invite with a Teams link and include a short agenda (15m narrative + 20m diagrams + 10m Q&A).

Appreciate it — Verdant Security
